payload.source_label: Equation (1.4): w_t + c w_x = 0 with c positive models a right-going one-way wave

contract.statement: In the one-dimensional constant-coefficient acoustic setting, a right-going sound wave with positive sound speed c is modeled by w_t + c w_x = 0. The source makes the acoustic variable concrete: if pressure perturbation p and particle velocity u satisfy p_t + K u_x = 0 and u_t + (1/rho) p_x = 0, with constant material coefficients and c = sqrt(K/rho), then w^1 = p + rho c u satisfies this right-going equation. The complementary combination w^2 = p - rho c u satisfies w^2_t - c w^2_x = 0 and describes leftward propagation. These are the two scalar modes of the full acoustic system [raw PDF page 24, printed page 2, equations (1.4)–(1.6) and following constructions; raw PDF page 25, printed page 3, opening paragraph].
assumptions: The physical setting is sound propagation along a one-dimensional medium, with the selected mode traveling to the right at speed c > 0 [raw PDF page 24, printed page 2, opening paragraph and introduction to equation (1.5)].

For the explicit construction of the acoustic variable, p and u satisfy p_t + K u_x = 0 and u_t + (1/rho) p_x = 0 [raw PDF page 24, printed page 2, equation (1.5), inherited by the construction following equation (1.6)].
K and rho are constant, and c = sqrt(K/rho) [raw PDF page 24, printed page 2, parameter description following equation (1.5) and definition following equation (1.6)].
The discussion inherits the constant-coefficient real linear first-order PDE setting [raw PDF page 23, printed page 1, equation (1.1); raw PDF page 24, printed page 2, equation (1.6)].

Existence of the partial derivatives needed for the displayed classical equations and linear combinations is implicit; no explicit regularity class is supplied [raw PDF page 24, printed page 2, equation (1.5) and the claim that w^1 satisfies its equation].

The passage presents a modeling statement and a conditional calculation from the acoustic system, without explicit formal quantifier syntax [raw PDF page 24, printed page 2, opening paragraph and construction following equation (1.6)].
quantifiers: x and t denote the spatial and temporal real variables, inherited from the introductory setting of equation (1.1) [raw PDF page 23, printed page 1, paragraph defining q].
p(x,t) and u(x,t) are the scalar pressure perturbation and particle-velocity unknowns of the one-dimensional acoustic system [raw PDF page 24, printed page 2, equation (1.5) and following paragraph].
K and rho are constant material parameters, respectively bulk modulus of compressibility and density [raw PDF page 24, printed page 2, paragraph following equation (1.5)].

c is the positive rightward sound speed, specialized to sqrt(K/rho) for the acoustic combination; w^1(x,t) is defined as p(x,t) + rho c u(x,t) [raw PDF page 24, printed page 2, equation (1.4) introduction and paragraph following equation (1.6)].
